chapters.title: Chapter 3: Form 26AS, Your Tax Credit Statement

lessons.title: Missing or Wrong TDS: Getting the Deductor to Fix It

children.text: Kunal, a relationship manager at a private bank in Indore, lays his Form 16 next to his Form 26AS in late June 2026. His employer deducted ₹8,000 every month, ₹96,000 for the year. Form 26AS shows ₹72,000. His cooperative bank FD paid ₹55,000 of interest with ₹5,500 of TDS, according to the bank's certificate, but that bank does not appear in Form 26AS at all. He is ₹29,500 short, and none of it is his mistake.
The frustrating truth is that Kunal cannot fix either problem himself. But he can diagnose it precisely, push the right people and protect his return while he waits.

body.text: Only the deductor can change what Form 26AS shows, and the department gives credit only for what Form 26AS shows. Your job is to make the deductor act before you file.

children.text: Step One: Diagnose the Problem
Every mismatch has a signature. Match what you see to the likely cause before you contact anyone, so your request is specific.

body.caption: Common TDS problems and what fixes them

cells: Deductor missing entirely
Wrong PAN quoted, or no statement filed
File a correction to update your PAN, or file the missing statement
Some quarters missing
Quarterly statement not filed or not yet processed
File the statement for that quarter
Amount lower than your certificate or payslips
Your entry left out or under-reported in the statement
File a correction adding or amending your deductee row
Status U (Unmatched)
Tax not deposited, or challan details quoted wrongly
Deposit the tax, or correct the challan details
Status O (Overbooked)
More claimed against a challan than was paid
Reduce the claim, or deposit the shortfall
Wrong section or wrong year
Payment misclassified in the statement
File a correction to the deductee details
An entry that is not yours
Someone else's deductor quoted your PAN by mistake
That deductor must correct the PAN. Do not claim the credit.

body.title: The correction types deductors file on TRACES

children.text: When you ask for a fix, it helps to know what the deductor's TDS team will actually file. Corrections are made through a correction statement on TRACES, and each type fixes a different kind of error. Several can be combined in one statement.

cells: C1
Deductor details, other than TAN
C2
Challan details, along with deductor details
C3
Deductee details such as amount, section or date, other than PAN
C4
Salary details, for salary statements only
C5
The deductee's PAN
C9
Adding a new challan and the deductions linked to it

children.text: Step Two: Build Your Evidence
A vague "my TDS is not showing" email goes to the bottom of the pile. A request with the TAN, quarter, amount and your PAN gets actioned.

body.title: Before you contact the deductor
steps: Download a fresh Form 26AS and save it as a PDF with today's date.
Note the deductor's name and TAN from Form 16, Form 16A or the bank's TDS certificate.
Identify exactly which quarters or transactions are missing or wrong, and the amounts.
Collect proof of deduction: payslips, Form 16 Part A, the bank's interest certificate or passbook entries.
Confirm your PAN is correct and operative on the e-filing portal.

children.text: Step Three: Ask the Deductor to Correct It

Write to the deductor, not just call. For an employer, that is HR or payroll. For a bank, it is your branch, followed by the bank's grievance email if the branch does not respond. Keep it short and specific.

body.title: A sample request you can adapt

children.text: Subject:
Correction of TDS statement for FY 2025-26, PAN ABCDE1234F
Dear Payroll Team,

My Form 16 for FY 2025-26 shows TDS of ₹96,000 deducted against TAN BPLX12345G. My Form 26AS for AY 2026-27, downloaded on 25 June 2026, shows only ₹72,000 against this TAN. The TDS of ₹24,000 for Q4 (January to March 2026) is missing.

Please check whether the Q4 statement was filed with my correct PAN, and file a correction statement if needed. I have attached my Form 16 Part A, my payslips for January to March 2026 and my Form 26AS. Please confirm once the correction is filed, so I can file my return with the full credit.
Regards, Kunal

body.text: Corrections do not show up instantly. After the deductor files, the statement has to be processed before Form 26AS updates. Ask the deductor for the date the correction was filed, then re-download Form 26AS every week or so until it appears.

body.label: Time limit for correction statements
body.value: 6 years from the end of the financial year
body.context: Introduced by the Finance (No. 2) Act, 2024. After that, a deductor can no longer file a correction for that year, so do not let old errors sit.

children.text: Step Four: Escalate If Nothing Happens
If the deductor ignores you, you still have options.
Follow up in writing
with a clear deadline, copying a senior HR or branch contact.
Raise a grievance on the e-filing portal
through e-Nivaran, attaching your Form 26AS, the deductor's certificate or your payslips, and your correspondence with the deductor.
Contact CPC-TDS
, the centre that processes TDS statements, on its toll-free number 1800-103-0344 or at contactus@tdscpc.gov.in, quoting the deductor's TAN.
None of these can force the correction instantly, but they create a record that you acted, which matters if a demand is raised later.
Step Five: Protect Your Return While You Wait
The due date will not wait for your employer. You have two reasonable paths.

body.title: Filing when TDS is still missing

columns.label: Wait for the correction, then file
points: Best when the due date is still weeks away and the deductor has confirmed it filed a correction
Your return matches Form 26AS on the first attempt
Risk: missing the due date, which rules out the old regime for FY 2025-26 and brings late fees

columns.label: File on time with the credit Form 26AS shows
points: Best when the deductor is slow or unresponsive
Report all income, but claim only the TDS that currently appears
Pay any resulting balance, then revise the return or seek a refund once the correction appears, within the time allowed

body.text: Do not claim TDS in your return that is not in Form 26AS and hope for the best. Automated processing will simply not allow the credit, and you will get an intimation with a tax demand. It is cleaner to claim what is visible and revise later.

children.text: If the problem is TDS that was deducted from your salary but never deposited, remember the protection from Chapter 2: under section 401 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (section 205 of the 1961 Act), you cannot be made to pay tax that was already deducted from your income. Keep the payslips and your correspondence. They are your defence against any demand.
A Special Case: TDS at 20% Because Your PAN Was Inoperative

If your PAN is not linked with Aadhaar, it becomes inoperative. Deductors must then treat you as if you had not given a PAN and deduct TDS at the higher rate under section 206AA of the 1961 Act, generally 20%. This is not an error the deductor can correct, because it deducted exactly what the law required at the time.

The fix is on your side: link PAN and Aadhaar so the PAN becomes operative again, then claim the full TDS shown in Form 26AS in your return. If the TDS is more than your actual tax, the excess comes back as a refund.
Check Your Understanding

body.title: Kunal's shortfall
body.prompt: Kunal's employer deducted ₹8,000 a month for 12 months, but Form 26AS shows only ₹72,000 against the employer. His cooperative bank deducted ₹5,500 on FD interest, which is missing from Form 26AS entirely. How much TDS is missing from his Form 26AS in total?
body.explanation: Employer: ₹96,000 deducted minus ₹72,000 shown = ₹24,000, which is exactly the Q4 amount of 3 × ₹8,000. Bank: ₹5,500. Total missing: ₹29,500.

body.title: Which correction?
body.question: Kunal's cooperative bank confirms it typed one character of his PAN wrongly in its TDS statement. Which correction type should the bank file?
body.explanation: C5 is the correction for updating the deductee's PAN. C3 covers other deductee details but specifically excludes PAN.

body.title: Where to escalate
body.textWithBlank: If a deductor ignores your requests, you can raise a grievance on the income tax e-filing portal through the ___ facility.
body.explanation: e-Nivaran is the grievance facility on the e-filing portal. Attach Form 26AS, proof of deduction and your correspondence with the deductor.

body.title: The cost of an inoperative PAN
body.prompt: Zoya, a schoolteacher in Lucknow, earned ₹80,000 of FD interest in FY 2025-26 while her PAN was inoperative, so the bank deducted TDS at 20% instead of 10%. How much extra TDS was deducted compared with the normal rate?
body.explanation: At 20%, TDS is ₹16,000. At the normal 10%, it would have been ₹8,000. The extra ₹8,000 is not lost: once her PAN is operative, she claims the full ₹16,000 credit in her return, and anything above her actual tax is refunded.

body.title: The entry that is not yours
body.scenario: Harsh, a software tester in Nagpur, finds an entry in his Form 26AS Part I from a Delhi-based consultancy he has never worked with: ₹3,00,000 paid under section 194J with TDS of ₹30,000. The ₹30,000 would reduce his tax bill nicely.
body.prompt: Should Harsh claim this TDS? What should he do about the entry?
body.modelAnswer: No. The credit belongs to someone else whose PAN was quoted wrongly, and claiming it would also mean the department treats ₹3,00,000 of professional fees as his income. If he claims the credit without reporting the income, processing will flag a mismatch. If he reports it, he pays tax on income he never earned. He should not claim either the income or the credit. He can contact the consultancy using the TAN to ask it to correct the PAN, and use the AIS feedback facility to mark the entry as not his, which Chapter 4 covers. He should keep a note of what he did in case he receives a query.

points: Only the deductor can correct Form 26AS, and credit is given only for what Form 26AS shows.
Diagnose first: missing deductor, missing quarter, lower amount, U or O status, or an entry that is not yours.
Write to the deductor with the TAN, quarter, amount and your PAN, and attach proof of deduction.
Escalate through e-Nivaran on the e-filing portal or CPC-TDS if the deductor does not act.
File on time claiming the credit that is visible, then revise once the correction appears.
TDS at 20% because of an inoperative PAN is not a deductor error. Make your PAN operative and claim the full credit.

body.text: This lesson is for education only and reflects procedures as of September 2026. PANs, TANs and the sample email are illustrative. Helpline details and portal features can change, so check TRACES and the e-filing portal for current information, or consult a chartered accountant.
